versions.name: Camp Freedom

features.note: A campfire circle reached on foot from the camp parade field.
The camp runs its own aquatics program area rather than sharing one with its sibling camp on the reservation.
At the range and target activities area, which is shared with the neighbouring camp on the same reservation.
An on-property rider-course day trek run by the reservation's high-adventure staff, finishing with a ride around the lake.
Newer shower houses with twelve single-occupant rooms, each holding a shower, sink and toilet, plus older shower buildings in each camp.
Offered as a day-trek float of about fifteen miles on a nearby river rather than on the camp lake.
An off-property day trek descending an unlit natural cave system.
At the challenge course area, which is shared with the neighbouring camp on the same reservation.
Group initiative games, trust events and low and high course elements; the area is shared with the neighbouring camp on the same reservation.

A four-hundred-seat family-style dining hall with assigned tables and rotating waiters; this is what distinguishes the camp from its patrol-cooking sibling on the same reservation. One evening a week the hall closes and units cook a steak dinner over coals in their campsite.
A Trail to First Class program emphasising the patrol method, with Scouts also working several merit badges along the way.
On the reservation's own lake.
In the single-occupant shower rooms; campsites themselves are served by latrines.
Campers can bring hammocks and hang them among the trees at the campsite, unstacked.
The camp runs its own handicraft program area.
The reservation health lodge in the central service area, with health officers on call around the clock.
A day-trek program for Scouts aged fourteen and over, staged from the reservation's high-adventure base while they camp and eat with their troop.
Includes a five-mile trail circuit of the reservation lake.
A day-trek paddle on a nearby lake using camp kayaks.
A day trek on rented bikes at an off-property trail system built for progression.
At the shared ecology and STEM program area.
The day-trek track, open to Scouts aged fourteen and over.
Camp-provided canvas wall tents on wooden floorboards, with a cot per camper.
Part of the challenge course program.
At the shared range and target activities area.
A day trek on natural sandstone cliffs with instruction in movement, knots and belaying.
On the reservation's own lake.
The scoutcraft area is shared with the neighbouring camp on the same reservation.
The range and target activities area is shared with the neighbouring camp on the same reservation.
Offered as sporting clays on an off-property day trek to a nearby mountain resort.
A combined ecology and STEM area shared with the neighbouring camp on the same reservation.
On the reservation's own lake, which is wholly inside the property.
On the reservation's own lake.
A two-hundred-and-seventy-acre lake owned entirely by the reservation; campsites sit both on ridge tops and along the shore.
A guided day trek down seven and a half miles of class three whitewater.
A canopy zipline and high ropes day trek run with a university outdoor education partner.

versions.summary: Scouts BSA resident camp operated by Laurel Highlands Council at Heritage Reservation in Farmington, Pennsylvania, featuring a dining hall.

provenance.notes: Imported from camp-finder; raw description and sessions dropped (operational data stays at the council site). verified_at is camp-finder's own source-confirmation date; imported_at is when open-scout-api ingested it. The evergreen summary is original prose regenerated from that description, excluding dates/fees/schedules. camp_type classified from program_types.
